newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Kabila returns to Zaire after S.Africa talks.
newsitem.headline: Kabila returns to Zaire after S.Africa talks.

text.p: Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila left South Africa on Thursday morning after talks with President Nelson Mandela and U.N. special envoy Mohamed Sahnoun, officials said.
He left Cape Town on Thursday morning in a South African Air Force plane which was flying him back to Lubumbashi, a foreign ministry official said.
Sources said Kabila's return to Lubumbashi was a "positive development" and not a sign of any problems or breakdown.

Kabila, who arrived in Cape Town on Wednesday afternoon, met Mandela for about an hour and later held talks with Sahnoun, the special representative for the U.N. and the Organisation of African unity on a peace plan for Zaire.

"After Mr Kabila saw the president, the talks reconvened late last night with Deputy (Foreign) Minister Aziz Pahad and Sahnoun, and went on until (after midnight). It's part of the ongoing peace process, based on the U.N. peace plan," said the official, who acted as spokesman for the talks.

A senior South African government source said Mandela was looking for an accord which would not require President Mobutu Sese Seko's resignation as a precondition for a ceasefire in Zaire, half of which is now controlled by Kabila's rebels.
